groups.name: BIM authoring
groups.sub: Plans, sections, elevations and schedules drawn from one building model.

groups.name: 2D and 3D drafting
groups.sub: Plans and details drawn in DWG or DXF, shared as files and external references.

groups.name: 3D modeling
groups.sub: Massing, form and design studies by editing geometry directly.

groups.name: Task-specific modelers and simulators
groups.sub: Built for one job, such as framing, fabrication, interior layout or simulation.

groups.name: In the browser
groups.sub: Newer tools that run in a web browser, several people in one file.

tools.name: Revit
notes: RVT is the usual coordination format in US practice. Worksharing puts several people in one model on a local server. Cloud worksharing is a separate entitlement.
On a Mac it runs in a Windows virtual machine.
tools.meta: Price: $3,012 a year or $380 a month. AEC Collection $3,675 a year or $460 a month. Flex: $99 for 33 tokens, and Revit uses 10 tokens a day · Website

tools.name: Archicad
notes: Teamwork and BIMcloud put several people in one model.
Revit exchange carries 3D geometry, not an editable Revit project.
tools.meta: Price: Studio from $2,414 a year, Collaborate from $2,840 a year · Website

tools.name: Vectorworks Architect
notes: 2D drafting, 3D modeling and BIM in one app, also used for landscape and stage work. Project Sharing puts several people in one file.
It imports Revit projects and families but does not save RVT.
tools.meta: Price: Architect $1,530 a year or $170 a month. Design Suite, with landscape tools and library, $1,980 a year or $220 a month · Website

tools.name: Allplan
notes: Architecture and structure in one model, with reinforcement and precast detailing. Common in Germany and central Europe.
RVT import has version limits.
tools.meta: Price: Pro $3,588 a year · Website

tools.name: Chief Architect Premier
notes: Residential design: house plans, framing, roofs, cabinets, 3D views and permit sets. Home Designer is the consumer version.
It imports and exports DXF, DWG, 3DS, SKP, STL and DAE, but not IFC.
tools.meta: Price: $1,995 a year · Website

tools.name: BricsCAD BIM
notes: BIM that saves to DWG, with AutoCAD-style commands, built on BricsCAD Pro. The only BIM authoring app here that runs on Linux.
Revit files come in as geometry. Shared work is file-based.
tools.meta: Price: $1,166 a year or $2,616 perpetual · Website

tools.name: FreeCAD
notes: A parametric 3D modeler with a BIM workbench built in since version 1.0: walls, slabs, windows, stairs, spaces and schedules. It works on IFC files directly. Drawings are model views placed on TechDraw pages at scale.
DWG goes through an external converter, such as the ODA File Converter. There is no RVT import.
tools.meta: Price: Free, open source (LGPL) · Website

tools.name: Bonsai
notes: A Blender add-on that stores every object as IFC, so the IFC file is the project file. It adds schedules, quantities, costing, 4D scheduling and COBie.
Drawings are generated from the model as SVG, and its documentation calls the drafting tools early-stage. Merging other people’s changes needs the separate ifcmerge tool and is experimental.
tools.meta: Price: Free, open source · Bonsai Viewer, a standalone IFC viewer, is separate · Website

tools.name: OpenArch BIM
notes: BIM written from scratch in Rust. It models layered walls, floors, roofs and families, with plans, elevations, sections and schedules.
In early development, with no releases yet. Sheets and PDF, DXF and IFC export are planned.
tools.meta: Price: Free, open source (AGPL-3.0) · Website

tools.name: BIMopen
notes: A BIM modeler from one developer, written with Claude Code. Plans export as SVG, sheets as PDF, schedules as CSV and models as IFC4. It opens IFC2x3 and IFC4.
Ceilings, phases, loadable families and DWG export are still missing. The source is not public yet. The site is in Italian.
tools.meta: Price: Free · Also on Android · Website

tools.name: BimCraft
notes: Parametric walls, doors and windows on levels and grids, with views, schedules, sheets and clash checks, meant to feel familiar to Revit users. It does not open or save RVT.
It ships in CadCraft Studio with CadCraft, and early builds run in the browser. The downloads are not code-signed yet. Saving in the browser needs a paid team plan.
tools.meta: Price: Free, open source (Apache-2.0). SuperCad Studio, which is to combine the eight apps in one window, is a separate commercial product at $250 a seat · Also on Android · Website · Source

tools.name: Lapin
notes: BIM built on IFC from a small Romanian studio. It models walls, floors, roofs, stairs, structure and MEP schematics, with sections, elevations and sheets printed to PDF or DXF, and it reads and writes IFC4 and IFC4X3.
A host shares the open project and others join live from the app or a browser. DWG must be saved as DXF first. The browser version runs the same app, a little slower than the desktop one.
tools.meta: Price: Free, open source (MIT) · Website

tools.name: AutoCAD
notes: Drafting and documentation in DWG, with shared work through files and external references.
The Mac version lacks some Windows features and add-ons. The web and mobile apps have a reduced command set.
tools.meta: Price: $2,095 a year. AEC Collection $3,675 a year or $460 a month. Flex: AutoCAD uses 7 tokens a day. AutoCAD LT, 2D only, costs less · Website

tools.name: BricsCAD Lite / Pro
notes: DWG drafting with AutoCAD-style commands. Lite is 2D. Pro adds 3D modeling, point clouds and third-party apps.
IFC and Revit import are in BricsCAD BIM only.
tools.meta: Price: Lite $345 a year or $780 perpetual. Pro $780 a year or $1,752 perpetual · Website

tools.name: ZWCAD
notes: Standard covers 2D drafting, annotation and plotting in DWG. Professional adds 3D modeling, IFC editing and RVT import.
tools.meta: Price: Standard $899, Professional $1,399 perpetual · Website

tools.name: LibreCAD
notes: 2D drafting with layers, blocks, dimensions and hatches, printing to PDF and SVG.
DXF is its native format. It reads DWG, and saving DWG needs a build compiled with DWG support.
tools.meta: Price: Free, open source (GPLv2) · Website

tools.name: QCAD Community Edition
notes: 2D drafting with layers, blocks, dimensions, hatching and a large part library. The open-source Community Edition saves DXF.
DWG comes with QCAD Professional, a paid add-on. The download is the Professional trial, and removing the add-on leaves the Community Edition.
tools.meta: Price: Community Edition free, open source. Professional is a paid license · Website

tools.name: CadCraft
notes: Command-line 2D drafting with layers, blocks, dimensions and plottable layouts, meant to feel familiar to AutoCAD users. One of eight free apps from the same studio.
The apps ship together in CadCraft Studio, and early builds run in the browser. The downloads are not code-signed yet. Saving in the browser needs a paid team plan.
tools.meta: Price: Free, open source (Apache-2.0). SuperCad Studio, which is to combine the eight apps in one window, is a separate commercial product at $250 a seat · Also on Android · Website · Source

tools.name: FlatCad
notes: 2D drafting for laser cutting, CNC and floor plans, from one developer. It opens DXF, SVG, Illustrator and PDF files, exports DXF and SVG, and prints PDF at a true scale such as 1:50.
Its maker says it is not an architecture program, with no walls, storeys or furniture libraries. Drawings stay in the browser.
tools.meta: Price: Free · Website

tools.name: DraftSight
notes: DWG drafting with commands familiar from AutoCAD, including AutoLISP. Premium adds 3D modeling, custom blocks, the Sheet Set Manager and a BIM module that imports Revit and IFC models for plans, sections and elevations.
There is no longer a free version. Perpetual licenses are sold only through resellers.
tools.meta: Price: Professional $299 a year, Premium $599 a year, network licenses from $399 a year. A 30-day trial of Premium is free · How to buy · Website

tools.name: SketchUp Pro
notes: Surface modeling with a large library of models and extensions. LayOut turns model views into scaled, dimensioned sheets.
The Revit Importer runs on Windows, in eligible plans. Trimble Connect shares files, one person editing at a time.
tools.meta: Price: Pro $399 a year. Go and Studio plans are also offered · Website

tools.name: Rhino + Grasshopper
notes: NURBS modeling for freeform surfaces, with Grasshopper built in for parametric geometry. VisualARQ, a paid plug-in, adds BIM objects and IFC on Windows.
Rhino.Inside.Revit runs Rhino and Grasshopper inside Revit on Windows. Shared work runs through worksessions of linked files.
tools.meta: Price: $995 one-time, upgrade $595. A 90-day evaluation is free · Website

tools.name: Blender
notes: A general 3D modeler of meshes and curves, with its own renderer. It has no building objects, dimensions or sheets. Those come from the Bonsai add-on.
DXF import is a community extension. Mac builds need Apple silicon.
tools.meta: Price: Free, open source (GPL) · Website

tools.name: SketchUp Free
notes: SketchUp’s modeler in the browser, with 10 GB of Trimble Connect storage. There is no LayOut, so no sheets. DWG and other CAD formats need a paid plan.
Trimble’s terms limit free versions to non-commercial use.
tools.meta: Price: Free for non-commercial use · Terms · Website

tools.name: IngeTrazo
notes: A 3D modeler for architecture and engineering from Peru, with push-pull solids and typed lengths. An optional BIM layer, still in development, tags walls, slabs, columns and doors and exports IFC 4.
Sheets hold scaled views with dimensions tied to the model and print to vector PDF. DWG import does not work on Mac yet.
A built-in AI assistant runs on your own key, and an MCP bridge lets Claude draw in the open app.
tools.meta: Price: Free, open source (GPL-3.0), with no paid editions · Website · Source

tools.name: Tinkercad
notes: Beginner 3D modeling by combining and subtracting basic shapes. It exports STL, OBJ, glTF and SVG, and imports STL, OBJ and SVG.
Invited collaborators edit the same design at the same time.
tools.meta: Price: Free · Website

tools.name: Plasticity
notes: Solid and surface modeling for product, vehicle and game design, built on the Parasolid kernel. It edits geometry directly, with no history tree. It has no building objects or sheets.

Hidden-line export makes SVG drawings from a model. DWG and DXF import is in the Studio license, on Windows only. Each license includes 12 months of updates, and companies with more than 10 employees need Studio.
tools.meta: Price: Indie $175 one-time, Studio $299 one-time. A 30-day trial is free for non-commercial use · Pricing · Website

tools.name: MoI (Moment of Inspiration)
notes: NURBS modeling built around 2D curves and booleans, from a single developer. It exports meshes, including n-gons, for rendering and 3D printing, and 3DM, STEP and IGES for other CAD tools. It has no building objects or sheets.
Version 5 is in beta for license holders, announced on the MoI forum. One license covers both the Windows and Mac versions.
tools.meta: Price: $295 one-time, upgrade from any earlier version $100. A 90-day trial is free · Purchase · Version 5 beta · Website

tools.name: AXIONBIM
notes: Light steel framing for prefab buildings. It frames wall, floor and roof panels from a DXF plan to your company’s framing rules, lays out roof and wall cladding, and writes machine files for roll-forming lines. Quantities, quotes and drawing sheets come from the same model.
It does no structural analysis. The model goes to an analysis program as IFC. Howick and AFF machine files are marked experimental. The interface is in English and Turkish.
tools.meta: Price: on request, yearly per license, in four plans. A 7-day trial of the top plan needs no card · Pricing · Website

tools.name: LumberCAD
notes: Plans builds in dimensional lumber, for people without CAD experience, from the Framexpert team. Parts snap together from a catalog of more than 300 components, the cut list splits parts into stock lengths and works out the cuts, and a documentation builder makes PDF plans with views, elevations, dimensions and material lists.

It exports STEP, OBJ, STL, DXF and GLB. Builds are private unless shared, and a shared link lets others view or copy a build but not change it. It does no structural analysis. Windows and Mac downloads are listed as coming soon.
tools.meta: Price: Free during the public beta, which is expected to run until early 2027. The price after it is undecided · About the beta · Website

tools.name: Sweet Home 3D
notes: Home and interior layout: walls, rooms, doors and windows in plan, furniture from a library, and a 3D view that updates. Plans export to PDF and vector images, the model to OBJ.
The desktop and browser versions are free and open source. The mobile app is paid.
tools.meta: Price: Free, open source (GPL). Mobile app paid · Website

tools.name: Motif Design
notes: Browser BIM and drawing sets, with AI agents that work in the same model as the team. Access follows a demo request.
Revit and Rhino models stream in, and IFC files import. Nothing exports back to Revit yet. Motif Review is a separate product.
tools.meta: Price: Design $150 a month, Review $25 a month · Website

tools.name: Qonic
notes: Opens large RVT and IFC models in the browser for coordination, quantities and editing. A Revit plugin moves changes both ways.
Since April 2026 it draws annotated plans and sections that update with the model and export to DWG.
tools.meta: Price: depends on configuration. The full configuration is $240 a month or $2,582 a year · Website

tools.name: Forma
notes: Site analysis and schematic design. Building Design, added in April 2026, is included with Revit and the AEC Collection.
Autodesk says Forma will replace Revit over time, with no date. It does not draw construction documents.
tools.meta: Price: $700 a year. Flex: 6 tokens a day · Website

tools.name: Snaptrude
notes: Concept to schematic design. Models start from a brief or a sketch, drawings update live, and several people work in one model at once.
Snaptrude describes Revit exchange as two-way. Its pages and release notes differ on how.
tools.meta: Price: Solo $60 a month, Organization $100 a month · Website

tools.name: Arcol
notes: Massing, floor plans, area metrics and presentation boards in one shared file.
DWG and DXF import as references to trace over, and IFC imports. Exports are GLB, STL and CSV, plus massing to Revit through an add-in on paid plans.
tools.meta: Price: $100 a month · Website

tools.name: Rayon
notes: Shared 2D plans for interiors and space planning. It imports DWG, DXF and PDF, and several people edit one file at once.
Rayon says version 4, due by the end of 2026, adds 3D.
tools.meta: Price: $21 a month, with DWG $38 a month · Website
